title: Workspace Mosaic & Anchored Sidebar: Prototype for Fast Route Discovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams struggle to find and switch contexts quickly across workspaces and related dashboards (rollouts, cost views, model routes) when their workflows span several products and projects. The current left rail is long and flat; it forces deep scanning, disrupts mental model, and fragments related surfaces (dashboards, rollout controls, cost breakdowns).

Goal: Design and validate an alternative information architecture that surfaces high-value routes and related surfaces with fewer clicks. Deliver a visual prototype (Figma) and an interactive InVision/HTML prototype for unmoderated testing. The solution should reduce time-to-route-find by 30% in usability tests, preserve discoverability, and integrate with rollout and cost-lens contexts.

Proposal summary: Introduce a Workspace Mosaic — a compact tiled view that groups related workspaces, recent routes, and pinned dashboards in a single, horizontally-scrollable module. Pair the mosaic with an Anchored Sidebar: a two-layer left rail where the top layer contains condensed, role-aware tiles and the bottom layer expands contextually into a route rail for the selected tile. Key interactions: quick-switch (keyboard + hover preview), predictive route suggestions based on recent activity and console telemetry, and an explicit "pin to mosaic" affordance for team-favorites.

Scope and constraints: This ticket covers the IA, visual patterns, prototype screens for desktop (>=1280px), and a short run of usability tests (10 moderated sessions + 50 unmoderated). Mobile and very small viewports are out of scope for this iteration; accessibility (keyboard, screen reader) must be included for the desktop patterns. Engineering constraints: must be implementable within the current Console layout grid and use existing token system. Performance note: the mosaic must render quickly (<100ms LCP) and avoid heavy synchronous network calls (client-side caching + telemetry prefetch suggested).

Trade-offs considered: 1) Putting more content in the left rail increases cognitive density but reduces vertical scrolling; we mitigate with progressive disclosure and role filtering. 2) Predictive suggestions risk surface churn — mitigated with an opt-out and a persistent history tab. 3) Tile-first navigation may obscure traditional project hierarchy; we retain an explicit hierarchy switcher in the top-left and breadcrumb lane in expanded mode.

Deliverables: Figma file with flow states (mosaic collapsed/expanded, pinned state, hover previews), interactive HTML prototype (links below), annotated Confluence PRD with acceptance criteria and telemetry plan, usability test script and results summary, and a short dev-handoff pack with CSS tokens and animation specs.

Acceptance criteria: see list below for measurable targets and UX sign-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates mosaic + anchored sidebar flows for at least three user scenarios: (1) switch workspace to a rollout, (2) open a cost breakdown view for a model route, (3) pin/unpin a dashboard to mosaic.
Moderated usability testing (10 sessions) shows median time-to-first-route < 6s and reduction in clicks vs baseline by >=30%.
Interactive prototype includes keyboard-only navigation and ARIA labels for all mosaic controls; screen reader walkthrough recorded and validated.
Design tokens and motion specs provided; engineering dev-handoff includes code-ready CSS variables and a recommended component API sketch.
Telemetry spec lists 6 signals (tile_click, tile_pin, route_open, suggestion_impression, suggestion_click, quick_switch_kb) and mapping to existing analytics dashboard.
PM and Eng have reviewed trade-offs and added acceptance for fallback to classic rail when user opts out or on small viewports.
